title: Land Finder
oneLine: A tool that scores rural parcels in two North Idaho counties on privacy, beauty, buildability and access, so a buyer can find good land nobody else noticed.

hero.alt: Generated stand-in image for Land Finder ("something"). Not a photograph of the real build.

intake.question: What is it, in one sentence?
intake.draft: A land discovery tool for Bonner and Boundary counties in North Idaho that scores rural parcels on how private, beautiful, buildable and recreation-adjacent they are, so a buyer can find good land nobody else noticed. Your own README line is the tagline: find land nobody else noticed.

intake.question: Role, timeline, status
intake.hint: Active, parked, or being shown to investors?
intake.draft: Solo. 1 commit, 8 May 2026, but the commit count is misleading: 25 source files and about 2,700 lines. NEEDS YOU: is this active, parked, or something you are showing to the land investors you have been talking to?

intake.question: What made it hard?
intake.hint: The scoring weights or the GIS pipeline. Which.
intake.draft: The interesting hard part is visible in scoring.ts: turning subjective ideas like privacy and beauty into numbers a computer can rank, from public GIS layers. Every weight in that file is a judgment call you had to defend to yourself. Second candidate is the geospatial pipeline, going from county shapefiles to PostGIS polygons to enrichment from USGS DEM, NLCD canopy and PAD-US.

intake.question: What did you decide, and what did you reject?
intake.hint: Why graceful degradation, and why MapLibre over Mapbox.
intake.draft: Two good ones are already in the code. First, everything degrades: no Supabase and it runs on curated local parcels, no OpenAI key and a deterministic regex parser handles natural-language search, and every parcel ships a baked-in summary so the drawer is never empty. That is a deliberate design stance and most people do not build that way. Second, MapLibre with OSM and Esri tiles instead of Mapbox, which means no key and no per-load cost. Say why on both.

intake.question: What number can you put on it?
intake.hint: Real parcel count once you import. That is the unlock.
intake.draft: From the repo: about 2,700 lines across 25 files, 4 scoring dimensions with documented weights, roughly 50 curated parcels, 2 counties, PostGIS schema with spatial indexes. NEEDS YOU, and this is the number that changes everything: how many real parcels once you run the importer against the actual Bonner and Boundary GIS data?

intake.question: What broke, and what did you do?
intake.hint: A parcel the model scored badly wrong.
intake.draft: NEEDS YOU. Anything in the shapefile import or the scoring that produced obviously wrong answers is a great story, because a scoring model that ranked a swamp as beautiful is the kind of failure people remember.

intake.question: What media do you have?
intake.draft: NEEDS YOU: a screen recording of the map with the drawer open on a high-scoring parcel. Geospatial work photographs better than any other kind of software, and this is the one project where a screenshot genuinely sells it.

intake.question: What would you do differently?
intake.hint: Two sentences. Not self criticism, a design judgement you would make differently now.
